title: Short Stuff: Magnet Fishing
summary: Short Stuff episode on magnet fishing, the hobby of dropping a strong rope-tied magnet into rivers, canals, lakes, or off bridges and dragging it to pull up metal objects. The hosts cover the hobby's growth in the US during the pandemic and its longer popularity in Europe, the powerful neodymium magnets sold by Brute Magnetics in North Georgia (Clay Copeland) for about two hundred dollars, the rope and gear to bring, the finds people have pulled up (guns, bullets, a Tommy gun, scooters, shopping carts, a reported body with handcuffs), safety concerns about unexploded munitions, etiquette about leaving trash behind, and legality, including South Carolina's Underwater Antiquities Act. The episode closes with Josh's anecdote about a neighbor dumping a microwave into a creek.

segments.title: Childhood metal detecting and magnet fishing
segments.summary: Josh recalls his father's metal detecting hobby and says he was tempted to try magnet fishing after learning about it.

segments.title: What magnet fishing is and its growth
segments.summary: The hosts define magnet fishing as dragging a rope-tied strong magnet through water. They note its boom in the US during the pandemic and its longer popularity in Europe.

segments.title: Brute Magnetics and affordable magnets
segments.summary: Clay Copeland of Brute Magnetics in North Georgia sells neodymium magnets rated to pull over two thousand pounds for about two hundred dollars. The hosts discuss the price and the car-weight comparison.

segments.title: Gear: rope, knots, magnet design, and safety equipment
segments.summary: The hosts recommend strong knot-tying skills, a long nylon rope, and a streamlined magnet that avoids weeds. They also suggest a tetanus shot and gloves because of rusty objects.

segments.title: Etiquette, unexploded munitions, and notable finds
segments.summary: The hosts discuss leaving trash on riverbanks, reporting unexploded munitions, and finds including guns, bullets, a Tommy gun, scooters, shopping carts, and a reported body with handcuffs.

segments.title: Legality and a neighbor's dumped microwave
segments.summary: The hosts explain that South Carolina's Underwater Antiquities Act bars collecting with surface-deployed equipment, including magnets, and that Europe has more restrictions. Josh describes a neighbor dumping a microwave in a creek.

segments.title: Closing remarks and sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts summarize: check out Brute Magnetics, dispose of found trash responsibly, and end the short.
